body:
I ran more tests to investigate.

`get_rpc_config()` is exposed in GDScript on `Node` and `GDScript` instances. 
These methods return rpc configs of a single `Node` OR `GDScript` instance.
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/25a3c27c41ac32f65d8efb8a54b08ad88211a700/scene/main/node.cpp#L852-L853
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/25a3c27c41ac32f65d8efb8a54b08ad88211a700/modules/gdscript/gdscript.cpp#L925-L926

This internal function parses rpc configs of a Node and its attached GDScript. It seems to be called before any execution of a rpc call to ensure all rpcs are cached and callable.
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/25a3c27c41ac32f65d8efb8a54b08ad88211a700/modules/multiplayer/scene_rpc_interface.cpp#L102-L114
When this internal function is called, it returns a correct rpc_config because it's fetching attached GDScript rpc configs too.

However Godot doesn't call this when using `get_rpc_config()` from GDScript but one of `Node` **OR** `GDScript` methods, so we get only one of the configs.

To fix this issue we could use/expose `const SceneRPCInterface::RPCConfigCache &SceneRPCInterface::_get_node_config(const Node *p_node) ` as GDScript 
`get_rpc_config()` or re-implement in class methods to return both `Node` and attached `GDScript` configs.

Can reproduce in 4.4.1 and in 4.5-beta1 when `get_rpc_config` is changed to `get_node_rpc_config` (the method was renamed). 
However, this seems like intended behavior according to the documentation added in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/106848, it works properly with `get_script().get_rpc_config()`
